title: SETA shared sparse subspace + Mirror views

random_selection.live_conflict_check: git fetch origin --prune; no MA-297 branch found

hypothesis: After a fixed shared-sparse-subspace discovery step, a per-task Mirror coordinate over retained shared atoms preserves aligned tasks with lower serialized inference bytes than matched task-specific shared-basis coefficients; unrelated tasks require private residual capacity.
physical_object: One frozen shared linear map plus one discovered frozen sparse feature basis
mirror_coordinate: One learned rotation angle per task over a pair of shared sparse atoms
logical_multiplicity: Four sequential task-specific linear functions sharing the same sparse atoms
controls: shared discovered basis without task code (SETA-style shared-only)
ordinary per-task coefficients on the exact same shared atom pairs
task_stream: Five known tasks: task 0 establishes shared physical weights; four sequential tasks train with frozen base and frozen discovered basis. Aligned teachers are rotations of paired shared atoms; independent teachers have independently sampled maps. Task IDs supplied at inference and charged.

development.selection_metric: mean held-out task MSE at final task across methods and both task families; bytes and retention are preregistered tie-breakers

storage.authority: actual deterministic serialized inference payload bytes
storage.codec: binary tensor-record codec charges field names, method/task metadata, dtype, shape and raw bytes
storage.optimizer_state: reported separately as resumable checkpoint bytes

success_gate: On every fresh aligned world, Mirror mean seen-task MSE <=1.10x matched ordinary shared-basis coefficient control, prior-task MSE increase <=0.01, and incremental inference bytes <=0.5x coefficient control. Mirror-specific result additionally requires a quality/byte frontier improvement over that native coefficient control.
failure_gate: Mirror misses the aligned quality/retention gate or is not better than the same-basis ordinary coefficient control at matched bytes/compute.
boundaries: Does not reproduce SETA routing or its full sparse discovery algorithm
Independent tasks test the private-parameter boundary
